chunks: He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali reported to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abil Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Nu'man, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) who said to me:

O Abu al-Nu'man, let not the people deceive you about yourself, for the matter shall reach you without them. And do not waste your day in such and such frivolities, for with you is one who records everything against you. And do good, for I have not seen anything more demanding in pursuit, nor swifter in attainment, than a new good deed for an old sin.
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Surely good deeds remove evil deeds; this is a reminder for those who remember.'

key_terms.السَّيِّئَات: Al-Sayyi'at - Evil deeds: sinful acts that are blotted out by good deeds
key_terms.حَسَنَة: Hasanah - Good deed: a righteous act that brings reward and erases sins
key_terms.يُحْصِي: Yuhsi - He records/counts: referring to the recording angel who documents deeds

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about good deeds removing evil deeds and the verse from Surah Hud?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advises Abu al-Nu'man not to be deceived by people regarding his own soul, as divine reckoning reaches him directly. He warns against wasting one's day frivolously, as a recording angel accompanies him. He urges good deeds, stating he has seen nothing more effective in atoning for old sins than a new good deed, then quotes Quran 11:114.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 3. He said: ’Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali reported to me from Muhammad ibn ‘Ali, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abul Qasim from Muhammad ibn ‘Ali al-kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Nu’man, that: Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him told me:

"O Abu al-Nu’man, let no people deceive you about yourself, for what is destined will reach you without them. And do not spend your day over petty things, for the One Who records everything is (always) with you. Always do good deeds, for I do not know of quicker recompense for an old sin than the new good deed.
Indeed, Allah, Most High has said (in the Qur’an): ’Surely, the good deeds blot out the evil deeds; this is reminder for those who remember.’ (Hood, 11:4)"
